h: Making the most of your jump slot
p: A good trampoline session starts before you get through the door. Dress everyone in comfy, stretchy clothes with no zips or buckles, empty pockets and leave jewellery at home. Tie back long hair, and bring a drink, as all that jumping is thirsty work. Grip socks are usually bought on your first visit and can be reused, so pop them somewhere safe for next time.

Get there a bit before your slot starts. Waivers, socks and the safety talk all take a few minutes, and you'll want every second of jump time once you're in. Listen to the staff briefing: one jumper per trampoline, no double bouncing and no flips unless you know what you're doing are the sort of rules that keep everyone safe and smiling.

Party planners, take note. Trampoline parks are a popular choice for birthdays because they burn off energy fast and keep a mixed group of kids happily busy. If you're booking for a crowd, give yourself plenty of notice and confirm exactly what's included, so there are no surprises on the day.
For younger children, quieter toddler sessions can be a much nicer introduction than a packed Saturday slot with bigger kids flying about. Look out for those if you've got little ones.

Once everyone's bounced themselves silly, High Wycombe has some nice ways to calm down. The National Trust's Hughenden, once home to Victorian Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli, is just north of town with grounds to explore, and West Wycombe's hilltop church and caves are only a short hop away.
